## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

input.body:
`packs/tidy-repo/tasks/improve-comments` declares `expected_outcome: 'open-pr'` and its worker doc forbids arming auto-merge, so every weekly comment sweep parks a PR waiting for a human — and the pass's own precondition then declines the next round while that PR stands.

Raise the ceiling to `merged-pr` and hand the PR to the shared delivery procedure (`packs/claudinite-tasks/deliver-pr.md`), so the repo's `maintenance.delivery` setting decides whether it lands unreviewed. The `improve-comments-scope` gate stays the safety case: it reds anything that is not comment text or `README.md` content.

Touches the task declaration, its `task.md`, the pack README row, the pack version + `VERSIONS.md`, and the test that pins the old ceiling.

attachment.snippet:
1	// tidy-repo task: improve-comments — the one tidy dimension whose subject is the
2	// repo's own source rather than its GitHub objects. The other three assess or act
3	// on issues, PRs and branches; this one reads a slice of the code AS COMMENTS and
4	// fixes what it finds there. Worker: task.md, which runs the improve-comments skill
5	// and nothing else.
6	//
7	// WHY IT IS A TASK AT ALL: a comment decays as the code around it changes and
8	// nothing makes it fail. No test goes red, no check fires, and no session working on
9	// something else will stop to fix one. The only way a repo's comments get read as
10	// comments is a pass whose whole job that is.
11	//
12	// WEEKLY. Comment drift is not latency-sensitive — a stale comment costs the next
13	// reader, whenever that is — and the window's commits are what name the files whose
14	// comments are likeliest wrong, so a weekly window is a bigger and better-targeted
15	// scope than a daily one for the same session cost.
16	//
17	// Self-contained (imports nothing): the whole contract is this default export.
18	
19	// The pinned commit subject the run's own scope gate keys on, stated in task.md and
20	// enforced by the skill's `improve-comments-scope` check. Kept in step by the
21	// declaration test beside this pack's other tests.
22	const RUN_TITLE = 'Claudinite tidy: improve comments';
23	
24	// How many of the window's changed files one round reads. A busy week can touch
25	// hundreds, and a session handed all of them skims; the rest are next round's, and
26	// the run says so rather than presenting a truncated list as the whole window.
27	const MAX_FILES = 40;
28	
29	export default {
30	  id: 'improve-comments',
31	  frequency: 'weekly',                   // the weekly anchor (DESIGN §2); the window's commits are the scope
32	  precondition_signals: ['commits', 'prs'],
33	  agent_model: 'opus',                   // whether a comment carries a why the code cannot state is the judgment here, and a wrong call lands in the repo's source
34	  // A ceiling, not a plan: the repo's own `maintenance.delivery` decides whether the
35	  // PR lands unreviewed, and a `review` member still gets it left open. What makes
36	  // the pass safe to land unattended is the scope gate — it strips the comments from
37	  // both sides of every changed file and reds anything else — so the diff can only
38	  // ever be comment text, and a wrong comment is a comment the next round rereads.
39	  expected_outcome: 'merged-pr',
40	  agent_instructions: 'task.md',
41	  agent_execution_timeout: 1800,
42	
43	  // Two gates, in order. Did anything land in the window — comments decay against
44	  // code, so a quiet week has nothing to re-read. Then: is this pass's previous PR
45	  // still open, in which case a second one would stack an unreviewed comment sweep
46	  // on an unreviewed comment sweep, over files the first one may already have
47	  // touched. Reading the pending PR's TITLE rather than a marker on the item means
48	  // a PR the owner opened by hand from this branch gates the round too.
49	  precondition(signals) {
50	    const openPrs = signals.prs?.open ?? [];
51	    const pending = openPrs.find((p) => String(p.title ?? '').startsWith(RUN_TITLE));
52	    if (pending) {
53	      return {
54	        run: false,
55	        reason: `PR #${pending.number} is this pass's previous round, still open — comments wait for its review rather than stack a second sweep on it`,
56	      };
57	    }
58	
59	    const commits = signals.commits;
60	    if (!commits?.substantiveChange) {
61	      return { run: false, reason: 'no substantive commit in the window — nothing moved for a comment to have drifted from' };
62	    }
63	    const touched = commits.touchedPaths ?? [];
64	    if (!touched.length) {
65	      return { run: false, reason: 'the window\'s commits name no changed path — nothing to read' };
66	    }
67	
68	    // A window can carry more files than one session should read as comments. Name
69	    // the cap and what it dropped rather than hand over a silently truncated list
70	    // that reads as the whole window.
71	    const scope = touched.slice(0, MAX_FILES);
72	    const dropped = touched.length - scope.length;
73	    return {
74	      run: true,
75	      reason: `${touched.length} path(s) changed in the window`,
76	      context: [
77	        `Read the comments in exactly these files, and no others: ${scope.join(', ')}.`,
78	        ...(dropped ? [`${dropped} further path(s) changed in the window and are NOT in scope this round — say so in the wrap-up so the next round is not read as a full sweep.`] : []),
79	        'A file whose comments are already right yields no edit — that is the common outcome and a good one.',
80	      ],
81	    };
82	  },
83	};

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

---
name: merge-to-main
description: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
---

# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`), body ending `Closes #<issue>`.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
6. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it again.
7. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.
